clue.text: Idiot born with a certain effervescence

blocks.note: b. is the abbreviation for born in dates and records
a certain one, as in 'one Mr Smith'
the froth on top of a poured beer

explanation.surface: Someone foolish is said to have arrived in the world fizzing with bubbles.
explanation.walkthrough: A head is the foam on a glass of beer, the effervescence that rises to the top.
explanation.definitionFit: A bonehead is informal slang for a stupid person, a straightforward synonym for a fool.

clue.text: Struggle with belief

blocks.note: to vie is to compete or struggle
w is a standard abbreviation for with

explanation.surface: Someone wrestling with their faith.
explanation.definitionFit: A view is an opinion or conviction someone holds, so it can stand for a belief.

clue.text: Strength of mollusc escaping trap

indicators.note: trap is slang for mouth, so words escaping it are spoken out loud

blocks.note: a mussel is a bivalve shellfish

explanation.surface: A shellfish shows its power by breaking free of a snare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trap' looks like a snare, but in British slang it is the mouth ('shut your trap'), so the mollusc is said rather than freed.
explanation.definitionFit: Muscle means physical power or force, as in 'putting some muscle into it'.

clue.text: European lady taking mum’s pulse

indicators.note: the lady takes in, or holds within herself, the word for mum

blocks.note: E is the abbreviation for European
a dame is a titled lady
ma is an informal word for mother

explanation.surface: A continental woman checks her mother's heartbeat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pulse' looks like a heartbeat but means an edible seed of a legume; EDAMAME are young soybeans.
explanation.definitionFit: Edamame are immature soybeans, and soya is a legume, whose edible seeds are called pulses.

clue.text: Allure of pharmacist dancing naked

indicators.note: naked means stripped of its covering, so the outside letters come off
dancing letters move about and change places

blocks.note: taken as written before it is stripped

explanation.surface: A chemist performing without clothes has a certain appeal.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the outer P and T from the fragment, then rearrange the remaining eight letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Charisma is compelling personal attractiveness or charm, which is what allure means.

clue.text: Ignoring pressure, Pat Cash prepared for action

indicators.note: ignoring the pressure means leaving out the letter that stands for it

blocks.note: p is the physics symbol for pressure
taken as written before the deletion
the ready is British slang for money in hand

explanation.surface: Pat Cash, the Australian Wimbledon champion, gets set to play while staying cool under pressure.
explanation.walkthrough: The tennis player's name is split: Pat loses its P, and Cash becomes the slang phrase 'the ready', meaning money.
explanation.definitionFit: At the ready means poised and available for immediate use, as a weapon held ready.

clue.text: Aims to support motor racing addicts

indicators.note: in a down entry the supporting word sits beneath, so it comes second

blocks.note: Formula One, written F1, with the digit read as the letter I
ends are aims or goals, as in ends and means

explanation.surface: Goals that help motorsport along.
explanation.walkthrough: F1 is the usual shorthand for Formula One; crosswords often let the digit 1 stand for the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: A fiend is informally an enthusiast or addict, as in a 'fresh-air fiend' or a 'drug fiend'.

clue.text: Crumbling bone found in barrow

indicators.note: something found in another is sitting inside it

blocks.note: a barrow is an ancient burial mound
a rib is a bone

explanation.surface: An archaeologist finds a decaying bone in an ancient grave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Barrow' suggests a wheelbarrow, but here it is a prehistoric burial mound.
explanation.definitionFit: Moribund means in terminal decline or near death, so it fits something crumbling away.

clue.text: Bombast of husband provoked a riot

indicators.note: a riot that is provoked is stirred up, so the letters are stirred too

blocks.note: h is the abbreviation for husband
taken as written before rearranging

explanation.surface: A husband's pompous speech stirs up a disturbance.
explanation.definitionFit: Hot air is empty, boastful talk, the same as pompous, inflated language.

clue.text: Some assume owls sound like cats

indicators.note: only some of the following letters are wanted, a run inside the words

blocks.note: the run straddles the two words

explanation.surface: A claim that owls hoot like felines.
explanation.definitionFit: To meow is to make the characteristic cry of a cat, a verb matching the definition.

clue.text: Grasp twisted hempen cord

indicators.note: twisting the strands of the cord rearranges their order

blocks.note: taken as written, all ten letters

explanation.surface: Take hold of a twisted rope made of hemp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grasp' looks physical, to hold the rope, but it means to understand.
explanation.definitionFit: To grasp an idea is to understand it fully, the same as comprehending it.

clue.text: Wish father to follow leads of distinguished elite

indicators.note: leads are what go in front, the first letters of the words
the father comes after the other part, so it is placed second

blocks.note: the opening letter of each word
to sire is to father, and a sire is a father, especially of an animal

explanation.surface: Someone hopes their father will join the upper classes.
explanation.definitionFit: Desire and wish are synonyms, both meaning a longing for something.

clue.text: Filling one’s head with nonsense and mischief

indicators.note: one item fills another when it is placed inside it

blocks.note: one's read as 'one is', so I'M
pish is an exclamation dismissing something as rubbish
a ness is a headland, as in Loch Ness or Dungeness

explanation.surface: A prankster stuffs their own mind full of silliness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One's head' looks like a single unit, but 'one's' means 'one is', and a headland is the head; the nonsense goes between the two.
explanation.definitionFit: Impishness is playful naughtiness, behaving like a little imp, which is mischief.

clue.text: Caution ex-PM, cycling on motorway in front of Tesla

indicators.note: cycling moves a letter round from one end of the name to the other
the front of a word is its opening letter
one part goes before the next in the order of the answer

blocks.note: the M1, Britain's first motorway, with the digit read as I
Liz Truss, briefly UK Prime Minister in 2022
its opening letter

explanation.surface: A former prime minister cycles along a motorway ahead of an electric car, which seems unwise.
explanation.walkthrough: The final S of the ex-PM's surname moves to the front; the M1 is the London-to-Leeds motorway.
explanation.definitionFit: Mistrust is suspicion or wariness, and caution likewise means a guarded, wary attitude.

clue.text: Head of Anatomy Department eviscerated lamprey with skill

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter
removing the guts leaves only the outside letters of the fish

blocks.note: its first letter
the usual abbreviation
only the outer letters remain

explanation.surface: A senior anatomist cleanly guts an eel-like fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head of Anatomy Department' reads as one job title, but only Head of governs Anatomy; Department is simply abbreviated.
explanation.definitionFit: Adeptly is an adverb meaning in a skilful, expert manner, matching the phrase.

clue.text: Hilarity left child with face flushed

indicators.note: flushing the face away removes the front letter

blocks.note: l is the abbreviation for left
a daughter is a female child

explanation.surface: A child runs off red-faced, leaving amusement behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flushed' looks like blushing, but it means washed away, so the child's first letter goes.
explanation.definitionFit: Laughter is the sound and expression of amusement, and hilarity is loud merriment or great amusement.

clue.text: Singing and strip poker after strong drink knocked back

indicators.note: knocked back means turned round backwards as well as drunk down
stripping the card game takes off its outer letters, leaving the middle
the card game comes after the drink in the answer

blocks.note: arak is a strong spirit distilled in the Middle East
the word with its outer letters removed

explanation.surface: A party where people sing and play strip poker after downing spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strip poker' looks like the party game, but strip is an instruction acting on poker.
explanation.definitionFit: Karaoke is amateur singing along to recorded backing tracks, a form of singing entertainment.

clue.text: Hearing vital flame is faint

indicators.note: on hearing the words, it is how they sound that matters

blocks.note: key means vital, and an old flame is a former lover

explanation.surface: Hearing that a crucial passion has gone dim.
explanation.walkthrough: Say 'key lover' quickly and it runs together into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To keel over is to collapse or fall down suddenly, which is what fainting does.

clue.text: Gentle, quivering embraces start to compensate for inattention

indicators.note: the start of the next word is its first letter
a quivering word shakes its letters out of order
to embrace is to hold something within your arms

blocks.note: taken as written before rearranging
its opening letter

explanation.surface: A soft, trembling hug makes up for being ignored.
explanation.definitionFit: Neglect is failure to give proper care or attention, which is inattention.

clue.text: Rubber blanket reused interminably

indicators.note: without terminals means both ends of the word are lost

blocks.note: blanket and mass as adjectives both mean wholesale, covering everything
taken as written before trimming

explanation.surface: A rubber sheet that is used again and again without end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rubber' suggests the material, but it means a person who rubs.
explanation.definitionFit: A masseuse is a woman who gives massages, literally someone who rubs people for a living.

clue.text: Retreat in silence, following alpha male on farm

indicators.note: the silence follows, so it comes after the first letter

blocks.note: alpha is the NATO and Greek name for the letter A
sh is the call for silence
a ram is a male sheep

explanation.surface: A dominant farmyard male withdraws quietly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Alpha male' reads as one phrase, but alpha supplies a letter and 'male on farm' is a separate animal.
explanation.definitionFit: An ashram is a Hindu religious retreat or hermitage where people withdraw for meditation.

clue.text: Poet in squalid room without alcohol

blocks.note: a dry event or place serves no alcohol
a den is a small, often untidy room or hideaway

explanation.surface: A writer living in a filthy, teetotal bedsit.
explanation.walkthrough: John Dryden was a 17th-century English poet and the first Poet Laureate.
explanation.definitionFit: John Dryden was a major English Restoration poet, so he is an example of the definition.

clue.text: Want touch of romance in the end

indicators.note: just a touch of a word is its first letter
one piece goes in, inside the other

blocks.note: its first letter
death is the end of life

explanation.surface: A wish for a little love before the finish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Want' looks like a verb, desire, but here it is the noun for lack.
explanation.definitionFit: Dearth is a scarcity or lack of something, and want as a noun also means lack.

clue.text: Result of shaving beard off a furry animal

blocks.note: removing a beard leaves the jaw exposed to the cold
taken as written

explanation.surface: A furry creature ends up looking very different after a close shave.
explanation.walkthrough: The playful wordplay: shave off your beard and you get a chilly jaw, a CHIN CHILL.
explanation.definitionFit: A chinchilla is a South American rodent prized for its extremely soft, dense fur.

clue.text: Retrospective benefit for apprentice

indicators.note: retrospective means looking backwards, so the word is read from its end

blocks.note: a boon is a benefit or blessing

explanation.surface: A backdated perk given to a trainee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retrospective benefit' looks like back pay, but retrospective acts on the benefit.
explanation.definitionFit: A noob is slang for a newcomer or novice, especially in gaming, so a learner like an apprentice.

clue.text: Emperor amid Eddystone Rocks

indicators.note: amid means in the middle of, so the letters sit within the words

blocks.note: the run straddles the two words

explanation.surface: A ruler stranded on the reef where the famous Eddystone lighthouse stands off Plymouth.
explanation.definitionFit: Nero was a Roman emperor of the first century, an example of the definition.

clue.text: Bears almost killed badger

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped

blocks.note: to bear is to have or carry
slew is the past tense of slay

explanation.surface: Bears nearly kill a badger, a woodland scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bears' and 'badger' look like animals, but bears is a verb and badger means to pester.
explanation.definitionFit: To hassle someone is to pester or harass them, which is what badgering means.

clue.text: Dismantled esoteric cabals

indicators.note: something dismantled is taken apart and can be rebuilt in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Secretive inner circles broken up.
explanation.definitionFit: A coterie is a small exclusive group with shared interests, close in sense to a cabal or clique.
